newsitem.title: INDIA: India govt stands by minimum alternate tax plan.
newsitem.headline: India govt stands by minimum alternate tax plan.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Monday rejected industry's opposition to a controversial proposed minimum alternate tax (mat) on zero tax rated companies, the Press Trust of India news agency reported.
"I don't know why the corporate sector should cry hoarse over this taxation," he told the Rajya Sabha (upper house) at the end of a debate on the general budget.
In his 1996/97 budget proposals made in July, Chidambaram imposed a minimum tax on high-growth companies that have earlier sought exemption from paying taxes by showing fresh capital expenditure.

"The corporate sector has to pay only 12.9 per cent as tax on the book profits while individuals earning over 10,000 rupees pay as high as 40 per cent tax. In fact, the corporate sector pays on an average an effective taxation rate of only 19 per cent," Chidambaram said.
The long-term solution to tax rationalisation lay in having uniform rate for the corporate sector, Chidambaram said, adding that a draft bill would be ready by December or January for discussion.
